content.thinking:
I'm planning to build the whole module in one pass, favoring robust primitives like lathe, extrude, sweep, and cards, while mostly skipping joints since parts aren't moving—though I need to check whether the builder still requires at least one root joint even with a static structure.

I'll go with a single root joint at the origin plus two hinge joints for the hanging lanterns, keeping the hierarchy simple. I'm scaling everything in meters: a torii roughly 3.2m tall with posts spaced 2.4m apart, a plinth base around 3.6x3m, the shrine set back, stone lanterns flanking at the sides, and a table up front. I'm now working out exact coordinates for the torii posts, kasagi, nuki beam, and where the hanging lanterns attach along the nuki ends, plus a helper function for creating boxes with position and bone attachment options.

Writing shader paint functions...

Building layered sweeps for the kasagi beam...

Now I'm adding the nuki crossbeam, a central gakuzuka strut with a gold four-petal emblem textured onto a plane, and a sagging shimenawa rope between the posts.

For the hanging elements, I'm figuring out zigzag shide paper strips extruded from a simple outline, and sketching hanging lanterns with cylindrical bodies that need a glowing paper texture wrapped around them.

Still designing scene geometry...

For the roof shape I'll stripe the paint with green tones for a tiled look. The lathe defaults to diamond orientation with 4 segments, so I need a 45-degree spin to get a proper square cross-section instead.

Now I'm planning the shrine details: stone steps, a wooden body with a paneled door and lattice, gold emblem, shimenawa rope with shide, and an offering table with cloth, fruit, a rice box, incense burner with smoke, and a flower vase. I'm also considering a maple tree built from a trunk sweep plus scattered red leaf cards using random frame placement, and finishing with stone slab ground tiles.

Now I'm sketching out the ground layer with mossy patches, scattered rocks, grass and fern cards, and fallen red leaves, then setting up base slab dimensions and working out how the torii posts should sit on top of the floor surface. I'm starting to write helper functions for creating a root joint and a reusable box-building utility to keep the scene code organized.

I'm double-checking my imports to avoid unused-variable errors, confirming which types and paint utilities I actually need from the parts and context modules. Now I'm defining color paints, like a weathered red tone built with grain and cel shading for the torii's wood texture.

Defining more paint constants...

I'm giving the shrine a dark wood grain texture, then designing an SVG flower emblem with four rotated petals around a cream center for decoration, planning to use a transparent background version for glowing lantern cutaways.

Making a reusable emblem function so I can generate orange, gold, and cream variants for different surfaces like the torii and cloth, plus sketching a red maple leaf SVG using a star-shaped path for additional decorative texture.

Skipping incense smoke for simplicity, I'll use a thin pale rising sweep curve instead. For the shide (zigzag paper streamer), I'm working out a lightning-bolt-shaped polygon outline that avoids self-intersection.

Writing the layout constants...

Placing shrine elements...

Still adding corner posts and door panels, then working out the roof lathe profile and apex height so the eaves extend past the body walls with proper radius, plus under-eave beam details.

Working out the roof slope normal and plane placement, I realize I need to correct for the fact that the profile radius refers to the corner, so the mid-face distance is foreshortened by a factor of 0.707 — recalculating the height and slope at that corrected distance.

Adjusting the position slightly along the normal for a subtle plane lift. Now I'm sketching the shrine's shimenawa rope with sagging and shide tassels across the front posts, then working out the torii post dimensions—tapered cylinders with a curved kasagi beam on top and nuki crossbeam placement.

I'm defining the post height and paint scheme, using a function that colors the lower portion black, a thin gold band, and the upper portion red, before moving on to the kasagi rings and gold banding details.

Now I'm laying out the nuki tie beam that passes through the posts, extending slightly beyond them with gold end caps, and planning a second tie beam positioned underneath.

Next I'm positioning the gakuzuka block between the nuki and the kasagi cap, plus placing a gold emblem plane on the front face of the kasagi, working out the exact y-coordinates so the red and black portions of the kasagi stack correctly.

Now I'm computing the curved shape of the kasagi's upward sweep using a parabolic path for both the red body and the black overhanging cap, then adding gold end-cap plates rotated at the tips of the beam.

Next I'm positioning the shimenawa rope with a catmull-rom curve strung between the posts, sagging slightly in front of the nuki beam.

Writing rope texture paint...

Now I'm laying out tassels at the center and sides, building lathe profiles that taper from a thin top into a bulging tassel body hanging down.

Next I'm positioning shide paper streamers along the rope, and adding hanging lanterns with hinge joints aimed downward on either side, keeping their parts attached to the bone positions.

Building lantern geometry...

Adding rib ring geometry and bottom cap details...

Lantern post sits outside the walkway posts, hung near the nuki beam. I'm laying out the stone lantern's parts stacked from a ground point G: a base plinth, octagonal post cylinder, a stone ring collar, and a firebox chamber above it, each with specific dimensions and vertical offsets.

For the firebox I'm giving it glowing window planes on its faces using a warm orange emblem texture, with thin stone mullion frames and a horizontal bar overlay, then capping it with a pyramid roof lathe shape that has flared eaves.

I'm adding a jeweled finial on top using a small lathe profile, bringing the total structure height to about G+1.3, with moss-tinted stone paint applied near the top surfaces. Then I'm scattering irregular flat-shaded icosahedron rocks around the base for a natural look.

Now I'm planning the perimeter stones -- a loop of roughly fourteen randomly-sized stone boxes placed along the edges of a 4.6 by 3.6 base plinth, with the torii positioned slightly forward of center.

Then I'm designing an offering table at the front: a red slab top with four legs, small gold corner caps, and a draped cloth runner hanging over the front edge.

Adding tabletop objects now: a plate with stacked persimmon spheres and a blue-green lathed vase shape on the cloth-covered table.

Positioning the rice sanbo at x=0.1 and incense burner at x=0.38. For the sanbo I'm building a wooden base box with a tray on top and a rounded white rice mound; for the incense burner I'm shaping a dark lathed bowl with thin tilted incense sticks whose tips glow orange, plus a wavy smoke trail rising above.

Now I'm adding a maple tree behind the torii post, sweeping a dark brown trunk with branch rods and scattering around 90 red/orange leaf cards across four foliage clusters using randomized frames and sizes, then placing small green bush/fern clusters nearby with randomly spun card frames.

I'm spreading fern cards radially using a golden-angle flow direction, then adding flat mossy ground discs near rocks and steps, red spider lily flower cards, and small mirrored fallen-leaf cards scattered on the pavement.

For the shrine structure, I'm detailing the cream wood base sill, red-painted posts and eave beam, lattice door panels in dark wood with a small gold emblem, and gold corner fittings under the eave, while skipping extras like ema plaques and handrails to keep things simpler.

For the 4 gold ridge rods running from apex to each corner, I'm checking that a straight chord sits slightly above the concave roof profile, which works fine as a ridge cap — raising a curved path through the key points by about 1.2cm to match.

I'm defining the roof tile pattern using a paint function with cell-based tiling, where cells with small distance differences get a dark teal color and others get noise-based variation between a few green tones.

Now I'm setting up the base pavement dimensions, edge fringe stones, color constants for black and gold, and grass tuft clusters at the base edges before writing the final TypeScript code for the builder.

Setting up imports and metadata...

Setting up the builder with a root joint and lantern hinge points, then defining a box helper for constructing the shrine's parts...

Still refining lathe point typing...

Now I'm placing the torii gate posts symmetrically with cylinders, adding a gold ring accent, and checking the vertical alignment between posts and kasagi so the overlaps look correct. I'm also considering adding a stone footing cylinder beneath each post to match the pedestal look.

For the kasagi, I'm building a curved sweep path using Catmull-Rom interpolation to form the gentle upward curve at the ends, then running into a typing issue with the radius function signature — it needs a tuple return type rather than a plain array, so I'm fixing that to properly define elliptical cross-section tapering instead of accidentally creating a linear radius taper.

I'm layering in a black cap sweep shifted along the normal, placing gold decorative end caps with slight rotation tilts, and now considering where to position an emblem plane on the kasagi's front face, near the red beam's center.

Next I'm building out the nuki crossbeam with gold end plates, adding kusabi wedge details at the posts in a dark reddish tone, then moving on to the shimenawa rope, hanging lanterns, and the main shrine body box dimensions.

Adding more door details...

Adjusting step positions so they nest within the platform without clashing, then checking torii post placement against the offering table width before positioning the stone lanterns at either side.

Now I'm placing the maple tree between the lantern and torii post, tracing its trunk curve upward and adding branch segments spreading outward at different heights.

Then I'm scattering leaf clusters around each branch tip, giving each cluster randomized leaf offsets and outward-facing orientations with some lean and bend for a natural look.

Now I'm placing decorative rocks near the base—a couple on the right front and one on the left—with varied sizes and slight height offsets to sit naturally on the plinth.

I'm looping to place border stones along the front edge as small boxes with slight random rotation and height variation, then setting up a tuft function to scatter fern-like card clusters across the ground for texture.

Adding ground flowers near the ferns, scattered fallen leaves across the pavement with randomized orientation, and an incense smoke trail rising with soft catmull curves and warm pale coloring.

Now I'm building helper functions for tassels using lathe geometry with outline points cast to the right coordinate type, plus a zigzag shide helper generating staggered left/right point lists for a lightning-bolt paper strip shape.

Writing stone lantern function...

Still working out the firebox dimensions and window frame posts...

Lantern top height checks out, roughly half the torii height. Now I'm sketching a window texture with a warm radial gradient for the glass panes, fading from pale yellow at center to amber at the edges.

Working out the emblem group, lantern stripes, and offering table geometry -- legs, top surface, apron trim, gold corner caps, and cloth draping.

Placing table items relative to the cloth boundaries: items within the central ±0.23 range sit on cloth, while wider items like the plate, vase, and incense fall on the bare table surface instead, each positioned at appropriate heights above the table top.

Now I'm building the flower arrangement sprouting from the vase: stems with varied tip offsets, thin green rods, and leaning flower cards at each tip with grass-leaf cards along the stems, plus flat-shaded persimmon spheres in orange. I'm noting everything needs baking through the cel paint pipeline, then moving to place moss discs near the rocks and steps.

With moss color variations layered and the border moss handled separately through stone paint, I'm estimating roughly 250 parts total, which feels sufficient. I'm deciding to skip extra details like ema plaques or bamboo for simplicity, but adding the nuki wedge post and lantern ribs, then positioning the hanging torii lanterns symmetrically along the nuki beam height.

Now I'm working out the precise lantern geometry -- hook ring height, cap and body dimensions, tassel length, emblem placement, and the lathe profile for the body outline with its subtle rib bulges.

I'm setting up the joint naming convention for the lantern bones (lanternL/lanternR at opposite sides), then defining helper functions for parts and planes with their fill colors and orientation options before writing out the full construction code.

Writing more helper utilities...

Still writing tassel geometry...
